items.definition:
to sell (goods), especially from a machine or stall
The machine vends snacks and drinks.

to state publicly or officially that something is true
She affirmed her commitment to the project.

to confuse completely
The complex instructions baffled the students.

To apply or bring to bear (a force, influence, or quality).
He had to exert a lot of effort to lift the heavy box.

To handle clumsily or ineffectively.
He fumbled with the keys before opening the door.

To obtain goods or a service from an outside or foreign supplier
Many companies outsource their customer service.

to visit again or reconsider
We should revisit this topic in our next meeting.

to make someone troubled or nervous; to stir up
The protestors continued to agitate for change.

to awaken or stimulate (a feeling or reaction)
The strange noise aroused his suspicion.

to wake up; to stir into action
The loud thunder awakened the sleeping child.

to state the opposite of
His actions contradict his words.

to treat or regard someone with contempt or disrespect; to break down or deteriorate
Pollution can degrade the quality of the environment.

to become progressively worse
The patient's condition began to deteriorate rapidly.

to expel someone from a property, especially with the support of the law
The landlord threatened to evict the tenants for not paying rent.

to set on fire
A single spark can ignite dry tinder.

to be more numerous than
The protesters greatly outnumber the police.

think about something carefully
She paused to ponder her next move.

feel or express sincere regret or remorse about one's wrongdoing
He truly repented for his mistakes.

return to (a previous state, practice, topic, etc.)
The system will revert to its previous settings.

break off (a meeting, legal case, or game) with the intention of resuming it later
The meeting was adjourned until next week.

To write or print a word with an initial capital letter; to take the chance to gain advantage from.
Remember to capitalize the first word of every sentence.

decorate with needlework
She decided to embroider a floral pattern onto the cushion.

apply a smooth, glossy coating
She decided to glaze the pottery before firing it.

make drunk or exhilarated
Alcohol can quickly intoxicate a person if consumed in large amounts.

to make random in order or arrangement
We need to randomize the order of the questions for the survey.

To swell or expand.
Eating too much can make you feel bloated.

To make someone very angry.
His rude comments enraged her.

To gradually wear away or destroy.
The constant wind and rain eroded the rock.

to produce and discharge
The sun emits light and heat.

to make someone a slave
Historically, powerful nations would often enslave conquered peoples.

to lose or be deprived of something as a penalty
If you don't pay the fine, you will forfeit your right to appeal.

to formally begin or introduce
The new president will inaugurate the peace talks next month.

to bite or pinch lightly; to stop something in its early stages
The dog gave a playful nip at my ankle.

to die, especially in a violent or sudden way
Many plants perish in the harsh winter conditions.

to raise; to improve morally or socially
Her inspiring speech helped to uplift everyone's spirits.

to administer a vaccine
Doctors recommend that children vaccinate against common diseases.

to go up or climb
The hot air balloon began to ascend slowly.

to support or strengthen
The new evidence will bolster the prosecution's case.

to take apart; to break down
The team had to dismantle the old machinery.

care for and encourage the growth or development of
Parents nurture their children with love and support.

make or become broader
Traveling can broaden your horizons.

praise formally or officially
I commend you for your hard work.

To interfere in something that is not one's concern.
Don't meddle in other people's affairs.

to leave a place that one previously occupied
Guests must vacate their rooms by 11 AM.

cause pain or suffering to; affect or trouble
The disease afflicts millions of people worldwide.

cause (someone) to feel isolated or estranged
His rude behavior alienated his friends.

confirm or settle (a bargain or an argument)
He managed to clinch the deal at the last minute.

to break into small pieces
The old wall began to crumble.

to hang loosely
The keys dangled from his hand.

to illegally seize or take control of
The terrorists attempted to hijack the plane.

to tell a story or describe events
She was asked to narrate the documentary.

to mean or indicate
What does this symbol signify?

to make someone feel anxious or uneasy
The news seemed to unsettle her.

to give a share
They decided to allot a specific budget for the project.

to add notes
Students were asked to annotate the text with their comments.

to block
Hair can easily clog the drain.

to make something legal
Many countries are considering whether to legalize certain drugs.

to repeat aloud from memory
The student was asked to recite a poem.

to build or form something again after it has been damaged or destroyed
The police tried to reconstruct the events of the crime.

to end or abandon something before its completion
The mission was aborted due to bad weather conditions.

bring or recall to the conscious mind
The old photographs evoked strong memories of her childhood.

be constantly or visibly anxious
Don't fret about the exam; you've studied hard.

cause to absorb water
It's important to hydrate well, especially during exercise.

to annoy by persistent fault-finding or requests
My mother always nags me to clean my room.
